questions.question: A company offers three types of successive discounts: First offer: 25% and 5%, Second offer: 20% and 10%, Third offer: 15% and 15%. Which offer is the best for a customer?
questions.questionHtml: A company offers three types of successive discounts: First offer: 25% and 5%, Second offer: 20% and 10%, Third offer: 15% and 15%. Which offer is the best for a customer?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the sum of successive discounts is constant (25+5 = 30, 20+10 = 30, 15+15 = 30), the discount is maximum when the difference between the two values is maximum.

Difference in First offer: |25 − 5| = 20

Difference in Second offer: |20 − 10| = 10

Difference in Third offer: |15 − 15| = 0

Since the difference is maximum in the First offer, it provides the highest discount for the customer.

∴ The correct answer is First offer.

Alternate Method

Given:

Offer 1: 25% and 5% | Offer 2: 20% and 10% | Offer 3: 15% and 15%

Formula for equivalent single discount of two successive discounts a% and b% = [a + b − (a × b)/100]%

⇒ Equivalent Discount for First offer = 25 + 5 − (25 × 5)/100 = 30 − 1.25 = 28.75%

⇒ Equivalent Discount for Second offer = 20 + 10 − (20 × 10)/100 = 30 − 2 = 28.00%

⇒ Equivalent Discount for Third offer = 15 + 15 − (15 × 15)/100 = 30 − 2.25 = 27.75%

⇒ Comparing the three values: 28.75% > 28.00% > 27.75%

∴ The correct answer is First offer.

Additional Information

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts x% and y%, the net discount is (x + y − xy/100)%. For three discounts, calculate the first two and then apply the result with the third one.

Customer vs Retailer Perspective

The best offer for a customer is the one with the highest net discount percentage, whereas the best offer for a retailer is the one with the lowest net discount percentage.

Relationship with Product of Discounts

When the sum (x+y) is constant, the discount is maximum when the product (xy) is minimum. In this question, 25 × 5 = 125 is the minimum product compared to 200 and 225.

questions.question: Four horses are tethered with a rope, half of the length of the side, at four corners of a square field of side 28m. What will be the area of the ungrazed part of the field?
questions.questionHtml: Four horses are tethered with a rope, half of the length of the side, at four corners of a square field of side 28m. What will be the area of the ungrazed part of the field?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of ungrazed part = Area of Square − Area of one full circle (as 4 quadrants of 90° form 1 circle).

Side of square (s) = 28 m, Radius of circle (r) = s ÷ 2 = 14 m.

Ungrazed Area = s2 − πr2

Ungrazed Area = 282 − (22 ÷ 7) × 14 × 14

Ungrazed Area = 784 − 616 = 168 m2.

∴ The correct answer is 168 m2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of the square field (s) = 28 m

Length of the rope (radius, r) = 28 ÷ 2 = 14 m

Formula Used:

Area of square = side × side

Area of quadrant = (1 ÷ 4) × π × r2

Calculations:

⇒ Total Area of the square field = 28 × 28 = 784 m2

⇒ Total Area grazed by 4 horses = 4 × Area of one quadrant

⇒ Grazed Area = 4 × (1 ÷ 4) × (22 ÷ 7) × 14 × 14

⇒ Grazed Area = (22 ÷ 7) × 196

⇒ Grazed Area = 22 × 28 = 616 m2

⇒ Ungrazed Part = Total Area − Grazed Area

⇒ Ungrazed Part = 784 − 616 = 168 m2

∴ The correct answer is 168 m2.

Additional Information

Area of a Square

The total space occupied by a square is given by Area = side × side (or s2).

Area of Circle and Sector

Area of a circle is πr2. For a sector with angle θ, the area is (θ ÷ 360) × πr2. Since square corners are 90°, each sector is exactly 1 ÷ 4 of a circle.

Combined Quadrant Rule

When four equal circles are drawn at the four corners of a square such that each touches two others, the radius is always half the side of the square.

questions.question: 4 × √{1296} + 4 × √{2116} + 4 × √{6561} - 10 × √{1225} = k. Then find the value of 'k'?
questions.questionHtml: 4 × √{1296} + 4 × √{2116} + 4 × √{6561} - 10 × √{1225} = k. Then find the value of 'k'?
questions.solution:
Given:

\(4 \times \sqrt{1296} + 4 \times \sqrt{2116} + 4 \times \sqrt{6561} - 10 \times \sqrt{1225} = k\)

Formula used:

\(\sqrt{1296} = 36, \sqrt{2116} = 46, \sqrt{6561} = 81, \sqrt{1225} = 35\)

Calculation:

\(k = 4 \times 36 + 4 \times 46 + 4 \times 81 - 10 \times 35\)

⇒ \(k = 4 \times (36 + 46 + 81) - 350\)

⇒ \(k = 4 \times 163 - 350\)

⇒ \(k = 652 - 350\)

⇒ \(k = 302\)

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: In a competitive examination held in the year 2000, a total of 6,00,000 (6.0 lakh) students appeared and 40% passed the examination. Forty percent (40%) of the total students. were females and the rest were males. The pass percentage among the males was 50%. Find the pass percentage among the females.
questions.questionHtml: In a competitive examination held in the year 2000, a total of 6,00,000 (6.0 lakh) students appeared and 40% passed the examination. Forty percent (40%) of the total students. were females and the rest were males. The pass percentage among the males was 50%. Find the pass percentage among the females.
questions.solution:
Out of 600000, 40% passed, the total number of passed students 600000 × 40/100 = 240000

Out of 600000, 40% were female, the total number of females = 240000 and males = 360000

The pass percentage among the males was 50%, total males passed= 360000/2 = 180000

So, female passed = (240000 - 180000) = 60000

So, female pass% = 60000/240000 × 100 = 25%

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs. 8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years 4 months, compound annually.
questions.questionHtml: Find the compound interest on Rs. 8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years 4 months, compound annually.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rate for 2 years = 15% p.a.; Rate for remaining 4 months = 15% × 4/12 = 5%.

Successive Multiplier Ratio: (20 → 23) × (20 → 23) × (20 → 21).

Total Principal Ratio = 20 × 20 × 20 = 8000 units.

Total Amount Ratio = 23 × 23 × 21 = 11109 units.

Compound Interest = 11109 − 8000 = 3109 units.

Given Principal = Rs 8000 ∴ 1 unit = Rs 1; CI = 3109 × 1 = Rs 3109.

∴ The correct answer is Rs 3109.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs 8000

Rate (R) = 15% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years 4 months = 21/3 years

Formula Used:

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)n × [1 + (R × t/12)/100]

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

Calculations:

⇒ Time = 2 years + 4/12 years = 2 years + 1/3 years

⇒ Amount = 8000 × (1 + 15/100)2 × [1 + (15 × 1/3)/100]

⇒ Amount = 8000 × (115/100) × (115/100) × (1 + 5/100)

⇒ Amount = 8000 × (23/20) × (23/20) × (21/20)

⇒ Amount = 8000 × (529/400) × (21/20)

⇒ Amount = 8000 × (11109/8000)

⇒ Amount = Rs 11109

⇒ CI = Amount − Principal

⇒ CI = 11109 − 8000

⇒ CI = Rs 3109

∴ The correct answer is Rs 3109.

Additional Information

Compound Interest for Fractional Years

When time is in the form a b/c years, Amount = P(1 + R/100)a × [1 + (R × b/c)/100].

Effective Rate of Interest

For two successive years with rates R1 and R2, the effective CI rate is R1 + R2 + (R1 × R2)/100.

CI vs SI Difference

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is P(R/100)2. For 3 years, it is P(R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

questions.question: The average of all prime numbers between 32 and 69 is:
questions.questionHtml: The average of all prime numbers between 32 and 69 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

List all prime numbers between 32 and 69: 37, 41, 43, 47, 53, 59, 61, 67.

Total count of prime numbers (n) = 8.

Sum using pairing: (37+67) + (41+61) + (43+59) + (47+53) = 104 + 102 + 102 + 100 = 408.

Average = Total Sum ÷ Count = 408 ÷ 8 = 51.

∴ The correct answer is 51.

Alternate Method

Given: Prime numbers between 32 and 69.

Formula: Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

⇒ Prime numbers between 32 and 69 are: 37, 41, 43, 47, 53, 59, 61, 67

⇒ Sum of primes = 37 + 41 + 43 + 47 + 53 + 59 + 61 + 67

⇒ Sum = 408

⇒ Total count of prime numbers = 8

⇒ Average = 408 ÷ 8

⇒ Average = 51

∴ The correct answer is 51.

Additional Information

Prime Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself. The only even prime number is 2.

Arithmetic Mean

For any set of numbers, Average = (Σx) ÷ n, where Σx is the sum of terms and n is the total number of terms.

Checking for Primes

To verify if a number N is prime, check its divisibility by prime numbers up to √N. If none divide N, then N is prime.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 2 : 3 and their product is 726. The smallest number between the two numbers is:
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of two numbers is 2 : 3 and their product is 726. The smallest number between the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of numbers = 2 : 3

Product of ratio parts = 2 × 3 = 6 units2

Value of 6 units2 = 726

1 unit2 = 726 ÷ 6 = 121

Multiplier (1 unit) = √121 = 11

Smallest number = 2 × 11 = 22

∴ The correct answer is 22.

Alternate Method

Given: Ratio = 2 : 3, Product = 726

Formula: Product of numbers = (First Part × x) × (Second Part × x)

Let the two numbers be 2x and 3x.

⇒ 2x × 3x = 726

⇒ 6x2 = 726

⇒ x2 = 726 ÷ 6

⇒ x2 = 121

⇒ x = √121

⇒ x = 11

Smallest number = 2x

⇒ 2 × 11 = 22

∴ The correct answer is 22.

Additional Information

Product of Ratios

When the product of two numbers in ratio a:b is given as P, the common multiplier x is found using x = √(P ÷ (a × b)).

Sum of Ratios

If the sum S is given, the multiplier x is simpler: x = S ÷ (a + b). No square root is required for sums.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by the formula √(a × b).

questions.question: In the given figure, ABCD and APQR are two parallelograms. If ∠ APQ = 100°, find ∠ CDR.
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, ABCD and APQR are two parallelograms. If ∠APQ = 100°, find ∠CDR.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In parallelogram APQR: consecutive angles are supplementary

⇒ ∠PAR = 180° − ∠APQ = 180° − 100° = 80°

In parallelogram ABCD: AB ∥ CD ⇒ ∠CDR = ∠PAR (corresponding angles)

⇒ ∠CDR = 80°

∴ The correct answer is 80°.

Alternate Method

Given:

ABCD and APQR are two parallelograms.

∠APQ = 100°

Formula used:

Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary.

Corresponding angles are equal when a transversal intersects two parallel lines.

Calculation:

In parallelogram APQR,

⇒ ∠APQ = 100°

⇒ ∠PAR = 180° − 100°

⇒ ∠PAR = 80°

In parallelogram ABCD,

⇒ AB ∥ CD

⇒ ∠PAR = ∠CDR

⇒ ∠CDR = 80°

∴ Option (2) is the correct answer.

Additional Information

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite sides are equal and parallel. Opposite angles are equal, and any two consecutive angles are supplementary (∠A + ∠B = 180°).

Diagonals of a Parallelogram

The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, meaning they divide each other into two equal parts at the point of intersection.

Area of a Parallelogram

The area is calculated as Base × Height. If two sides a, b and the included angle θ are known, Area = a × b × sin(θ).

questions.question: What is the sum of all the exterior angles taken in order of a triangle?
questions.questionHtml: What is the sum of all the exterior angles taken in order of a triangle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon, including a triangle, taken in order is always a constant 360°.

This is because walking around the exterior of any closed shape and returning to the starting direction completes exactly one full circle.

One full circle rotation is equivalent to 360°.

∴ The correct answer is 360°.

Alternate Method

Given: A triangle with internal angles A, B, and C.

Formula Used: Exterior angle + Interior angle = 180° (Linear Pair); Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°.

⇒ Let the three interior angles be A, B, and C.

⇒ We know that A + B + C = 180°.

⇒ Exterior angle at vertex A = 180° − A.

⇒ Exterior angle at vertex B = 180° − B.

⇒ Exterior angle at vertex C = 180° − C.

⇒ Sum of exterior angles = (180° − A) + (180° − B) + (180° − C).

⇒ Sum = (180° + 180° + 180°) − (A + B + C).

⇒ Sum = 540° − 180°.

⇒ Sum = 360°.

∴ The correct answer is 360°.

Additional Information

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon with n sides, the sum of its exterior angles (one at each vertex) is always 360°.

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of the interior angles of a polygon with n sides is calculated as (n − 2) × 180°.

Triangle Exterior Angle Property

An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles of the triangle.

Regular Polygons

In a regular polygon, each exterior angle is equal to 360° ÷ n, where n is the number of sides.

questions.question: A rectangular plot of grass is 80m long and 60 m broad. From the centre of each side a path of 3 metre wide goes across the centre of the opposite side. What is the area of these paths?
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular plot of grass is 80m long and 60 m broad. From the centre of each side a path of 3 metre wide goes across the centre of the opposite side. What is the area of these paths?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of two paths crossing at the center is given by the formula: Area = w(L + B − w).

Where w = width of path, L = length, B = breadth.

Given: L = 80 m, B = 60 m, w = 3 m.

Area = 3 × (80 + 60 − 3) = 3 × 137 = 411 sqm.

∴ The correct answer is 411 sqm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of the rectangular plot (L) = 80 m

Breadth of the rectangular plot (B) = 60 m

Width of each path (w) = 3 m

Formula Used:

Total Area of paths = (Area of horizontal path) + (Area of vertical path) − (Area of common intersection)

Calculations:

⇒ Area of the path parallel to the length = 80 m × 3 m = 240 sqm

⇒ Area of the path parallel to the breadth = 60 m × 3 m = 180 sqm

⇒ Area of the common square at the center = 3 m × 3 m = 9 sqm

⇒ Total Area of paths = 240 + 180 − 9

⇒ Total Area = 420 − 9 = 411 sqm

∴ The correct answer is 411 sqm.

Additional Information

Path Around Outside of Rectangle

Area of a path of width 'w' running outside a rectangle of length L and breadth B = 2w(L + B + 2w).

Path Inside the Rectangle

Area of a path of width 'w' running inside the boundary of a rectangle = 2w(L + B − 2w).

General Path Area Concept

When paths cross, the intersection area must be subtracted once because it is calculated twice in the individual path areas.

questions.question: A cylindrical tank of radius 14 cm is full of water. If 616 litres of water are drawn out, then the water level in the tank is dropped by ______ m. (Take π = (22/7) )
questions.questionHtml: A cylindrical tank of radius 14 cm is full of water. If 616 litres of water are drawn out, then the water level in the tank is dropped by ______ m. (Take π = (22/7) )
questions.solution:
Volume of water drawn out = πr2h

⇒ 616000 = (22/7) × 142 × h ⇒ 616000 = 616h

⇒ h = 616000 / 616 ⇒ h = 1000 cm = 10 m

questions.question: The angle of elevation of a cloud from a point 200 m above a lake is 30° and the angle of depression of its reflection in the lake is 60°. The height of the cloud is
questions.questionHtml: The angle of elevation of a cloud from a point 200 m above a lake is 30° and the angle of depression of its reflection in the lake is 60°. The height of the cloud is
questions.solution:
Let P be the cloud at a height H m above the level of the water in the lake 

Q be its image in the water.

⇒ BQ = BA = H and ∠ADP = 30° and ∠PDQ = 60°

In right-angled ΔADP,

⇒ \(tan30° = \frac{AP}{DP} = \frac{H - 200}{DP}\)⇒ \(\frac{1}{\sqrt3} = \frac{H - 200}{DP}\)⇒ DP = \(\sqrt3(H - 200)\) ----- (1)

In right angled ΔQPD

⇒ \(tan60° = \frac{PQ}{DP} = \frac{H + 200}{DP}\) ⇒\(\sqrt3 = \frac{H \ + \ 200}{\sqrt3(H\ - \ 200)}\)  [From equation (1)]

⇒ H + 200 = 3(H - 200) ⇒ H + 200 = 3H - 600 ⇒ 2H = 800 ⇒ H = 400 m

questions.question: The sum of digits of a two digit number is 8 and the difference between the number and that formed by reversing the digits is 18. What is the difference between the digits of the number?
questions.questionHtml: The sum of digits of a two digit number is 8 and the difference between the number and that formed by reversing the digits is 18. What is the difference between the digits of the number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be 10x + y, where x is the tens digit and y is the ones digit.

Given: x + y = 8 and (10x + y) - (10y + x) = 18.

From the second equation: (10x + y) - (10y + x) = 18

⇒ 10x + y - 10y - x = 18

⇒ 9x - 9y = 18

⇒ x - y = 2

questions.question: The marked price of a jacket is Rs. 3,500. A shopkeeper offers 5% discount on it and then again offers 15% discount on the new price, and then again offers 20% discount on the new price. How much one has to pay for it?
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of a jacket is Rs. 3,500. A shopkeeper offers 5% discount on it and then again offers 15% discount on the new price, and then again offers 20% discount on the new price. How much one has to pay for it?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply successive discounts directly using fraction multipliers:

SP = 3500 × 95% × 85% × 80%

SP = 3500 × 19/20 × 17/20 × 4/5

SP = (3500 ÷ 2000) × 19 × 17 × 4

SP = 7/4 × 1292 = 2261

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,261.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) of jacket = Rs. 3,500

Successive discounts = 5%, 15%, and 20%

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − d1)/100 × (100 − d2)/100 × (100 − d3)/100

Calculations:

⇒ SP = 3500 × (100 − 5)/100 × (100 − 15)/100 × (100 − 20)/100

⇒ SP = 3500 × 95/100 × 85/100 × 80/100

⇒ SP = 3500 × 19/20 × 17/20 × 4/5

⇒ SP = 3500 × (19 × 17 × 4) ÷ (20 × 20 × 5)

⇒ SP = 3500 × 1292 ÷ 2000

⇒ SP = (3500 ÷ 2000) × 1292

⇒ SP = 7/4 × 1292

⇒ SP = 7 × 323 = 2261

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,261.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP)

The marked price is the regular price tag printed on an item. Any discount given by a shopkeeper is always calculated on the MP, not the cost price.

Successive Discount Formula

When an article has multiple consecutive discounts, the net selling price is derived by multiplying the individual discount factors: SP = MP × (1 − d1/100) × (1 − d2/100) × ...

Equivalent Single Discount

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the effective single discount equivalent to both combined is calculated using the net change formula: (x + y − xy/100)%.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 9,350 was taken as a loan. This is paid in two equal instalments. If the rate of interest is 20% per annum compounded annually, then what is the value of each instalment?(approximately)
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 9,350 was taken as a loan. This is paid in two equal instalments. If the rate of interest is 20% per annum compounded annually, then what is the value of each instalment?(approximately)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rate 20% = 1/5 → Principal : Installment ratio for 1st year = 5 : 6

For 2nd year, square the ratios → Principal : Installment = 52 : 62 = 25 : 36

Equalize installments: Multiply 1st year ratio by 6 → (5 × 6) : (6 × 6) = 30 : 36

Total Principal units = 30 + 25 = 55 units

55 units = ₹9350 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹170

Value of each installment = 36 units = 36 × 170 = ₹6120

∴ The correct answer is ₹6120.

Alternate Method

Given:

Loan Amount (P) = ₹9350

Rate of Interest (R) = 20% per annum

Number of installments (n) = 2

Formula Used:

P = [x / (1 + R/100)1] + [x / (1 + R/100)2] + ... where x is the equal installment.

Calculations:

⇒ 9350 = x / (1 + 20/100) + x / (1 + 20/100)2

⇒ 9350 = x / (1.2) + x / (1.44)

⇒ 9350 = x / (6/5) + x / (36/25)

⇒ 9350 = 5x/6 + 25x/36

⇒ 9350 = (30x + 25x) / 36

⇒ 9350 = 55x / 36

⇒ x = (9350 × 36) / 55

⇒ x = 170 × 36

⇒ x = ₹6120

∴ The correct answer is ₹6120.

Additional Information

CI Installment General Formula

For n equal installments, P = x[1/(1+r) + 1/(1+r)2 + ... + 1/(1+r)n], where r is the rate per period in decimal.

SI vs CI Installments

In CI installments, interest is charged on the reducing balance (present value), whereas SI installments often involve interest on the total amount or specific due balances.

Effective Rate of Interest

If compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the number of periods is doubled (2n) in the installment formula.

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
questions.questionHtml: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total interest percentage = Rate × Time

Interest percentage = 3% × 6 = 18%

Simple Interest = 18% of 2500 = (18/100) × 2500

Simple Interest = 18 × 25 = 450

∴ The correct answer is ₹450.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹2500, Rate (R) = 3% per annum, Time (T) = 6 years.

Formula: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (2500 × 3 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (2500 × 18) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 25 × 18

⇒ SI = 450

∴ The correct answer is ₹450.

Additional Information

Total Amount (A)

The total amount to be repaid after the time period is the sum of the Principal and Simple Interest: A = P + SI.

Effective Rate of Interest

For simple interest, the total interest percentage over the entire duration is the product of the annual rate and the time in years (R × T).

Standard Units

Always ensure that the Time (T) is in years. If time is given in months, divide by 12; if in days, divide by 365 (or 366 for leap years).

questions.question: The age of some students is given in years as 12, 13, 16, 18,14, 19, 13, 17, 15 and 11. The median age (in years) of the students is:
questions.questionHtml: The age of some students is given in years as 12, 13, 16, 18,14, 19, 13, 17, 15 and 11. The median age (in years) of the students is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Arrange the given data in ascending order: 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19.

Since the number of terms n = 10 (even), the median is the simple average of the two middle terms.

Median = Average of the 5th and 6th terms.

Median = (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5.

∴ The correct answer is 14.5 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

The ages of 10 students (in years): 12, 13, 16, 18, 14, 19, 13, 17, 15, and 11.

Formula Used:

For an even number of observations n, Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

Calculation:

⇒ Total number of observations, n = 10 (even number).

⇒ First, sort the given ages in ascending order:

⇒ 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19

⇒ Median = [(10/2)th term + (10/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Median = [5th term + 6th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Here, the 5th term is 14, and the 6th term is 15.

⇒ Median = (14 + 15) ÷ 2

⇒ Median = 29 ÷ 2 = 14.5

∴ The correct answer is 14.5 years.

Additional Information

Mean

The mean is the simple average of a given set of numbers. It is calculated by Mean = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Median

The median is the exact middle value when a data set is ordered from least to greatest. If n is odd, Median = ((n+1)÷2)th term. If n is even, the Median is the average of the two central terms.

Mode

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A set of data may have one mode, multiple modes, or no mode at all.

Calculation:

\(45 - 22 \div 2 + 12 + 70 \div 35 + 0.4 \div 0.8 + 1.5 \div 3 + 1\)

⇒ \(45 - 11 + 12 + 2 + 0.5 + 0.5 + 1\)

⇒ \(34 + 12 + 2 + 1 + 1\)

⇒ \(50\)

∴ The correct answer is option (1).

questions.question: What is the value of \(\left(\mathrm{k}+\frac{1}{k}\right)\left(\mathrm{k}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{k}}\right)\left(\mathrm{k}^2+\frac{1}{\mathrm{k}^2}\right)\left(\mathrm{k}^4+\frac{1}{\mathrm{k}^4}\right)\) ?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of \(\left(\mathrm{k}+\frac{1}{k}\right)\left(\mathrm{k}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{k}}\right)\left(\mathrm{k}^2+\frac{1}{\mathrm{k}^2}\right)\left(\mathrm{k}^4+\frac{1}{\mathrm{k}^4}\right)\)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify the iterative use of the identity (a + b)(a − b) = a2 − b2.

Each product doubles the power of the variables and keeps the − sign.

The sequence of powers is: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8.

The final simplified form will be the square of the highest power terms in the last pair with a minus sign.

∴ The correct answer is k8 − 1/k8.

Alternate Method

Given Expression: (k + 1/k)(k − 1/k)(k2 + 1/k2)(k4 + 1/k4)

Formula Used: (a + b)(a − b) = a2 − b2

⇒ [(k + 1/k)(k − 1/k)] × (k2 + 1/k2) × (k4 + 1/k4)

⇒ (k2 − 1/k2) × (k2 + 1/k2) × (k4 + 1/k4)

⇒ [(k2 − 1/k2)(k2 + 1/k2)] × (k4 + 1/k4)

⇒ (k4 − 1/k4) × (k4 + 1/k4)

⇒ (k4)2 − (1/k4)2

⇒ k8 − 1/k8

∴ The correct answer is k8 − 1/k8.

Additional Information

Difference of Squares

The identity (a + b)(a − b) = a2 − b2 is fundamental for simplifying algebraic products involving conjugate pairs.

General Power Rule

For an expression of the form (x − y)(x + y)(x2 + y2)(x4 + y4)...(x2n−1 + y2n−1), the simplified result is x2n − y2n.

Cubic Identities

Sum of cubes: (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) = a3 + b3 and Difference of cubes: (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2) = a3 − b3.

questions.question: A sum of money doubled itself at certain rate of compound interest in 15 years. In how many years will it become four times of itself?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money doubled itself at certain rate of compound interest in 15 years. In how many years will it become four times of itself?
questions.solution:
Let the principle be P and the time at which the sum became four times be T

⇒ 2P = \(P × (1\ +\ {R\over 100})^{15}\)  ⇒ 2 = \((1\ +\ {R\over 100})^{15}\)      ----(1)

⇒ 4P = \(P × (1\ +\ {R\over 100})^T\) ⇒ 22 =  \((1\ +\ {R\over 100})^T\)     ----(2)

By equating (1) and (2) after squaring the eq (1),

⇒  (\( (1\ +\ {R\over 100})^{15}\))2 = \((1\ +\ {R\over 100})^T\) ⇒ \( (1\ +\ {R\over 100})^{30}\) = \( (1\ +\ {R\over 100})^{T}\)

By comparing the equations

⇒ T = 30 years

questions.question: Anil sells a table to Kamal at a profit of 10% and Kamal sells it to Rajat at a profit of 12%. If Rajat pays ₹246.40 for it, then how much had Anil paid for it?
questions.questionHtml: Anil sells a table to Kamal at a profit of 10% and Kamal sells it to Rajat at a profit of 12%. If Rajat pays ₹246.40 for it, then how much had Anil paid for it?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Anil to Kamal profit = 10% → Ratio = 10 : 11

Kamal to Rajat profit = 12% → Ratio = 25 : 28

Successive Ratio (Anil : Rajat) = (10 × 25) : (11 × 28) = 250 : 308

308 units = ₹246.40 ⇒ 1 unit = 0.8

Anil CP = 250 units × 0.8 = ₹200

∴ The correct answer is ₹200.

Alternate Method

Given:

Anil profit = 10%

Kamal profit = 12%

Rajat payment (Final SP) = ₹246.40

Calculations:

Let the cost price for Anil be ₹ x.

⇒ Price paid by Kamal = x × (100 + 10) ÷ 100 = 1.1x

⇒ Price paid by Rajat = 1.1x × (100 + 12) ÷ 100

⇒ 246.40 = 1.1x × 1.12

⇒ 246.40 = 1.232x

⇒ x = 246.40 ÷ 1.232

⇒ x = 200

∴ The correct answer is ₹200.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the effective change is [a + b + (a × b)/100] %.

Chain Selling Formula

Final Price = Initial CP × (100 ± P1/L1)/100 × (100 ± P2/L2)/100 × ...

Cost Price Calculation

CP = [SP ÷ (100 + Profit %)] × 100 or CP = [SP ÷ (100 − Loss %)] × 100.

questions.question: The speed of a boat down the stream is 125% of the speed in still water. If the boat takes 30 minutes to cover 20 km in still water, then how much time (in hours) will it take to cover 15 km upstream?
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a boat down the stream is 125% of the speed in still water. If the boat takes 30 minutes to cover 20 km in still water, then how much time (in hours) will it take to cover 15 km upstream?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed ratio Downstream : Still water = 125% : 100% = 5 : 4

Stream speed ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 part, so Upstream speed ratio = 4 − 1 = 3 parts.

Speed in still water (4 parts) = 20 km ÷ 0.5 hr = 40 km/h.

Upstream speed (3 parts) = (40 ÷ 4) × 3 = 30 km/h.

Time for 15 km upstream = 15 ÷ 30 = 1/2 hour.

∴ The correct answer is 1/2 hour.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Speed downstream = 125% of speed in still water.

⇒ Time taken to cover 20 km in still water = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours.

Formula Used:

⇒ Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = Boat Speed (B) + Stream Speed (S)

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = Boat Speed (B) − Stream Speed (S)

Calculations:

⇒ Speed in still water (B) = 20 km ÷ 0.5 hours = 40 km/h

⇒ Speed downstream (D) = 125% of 40 = 1.25 × 40 = 50 km/h

⇒ Speed of stream (S) = D − B = 50 − 40 = 10 km/h

⇒ Speed upstream (U) = B − S = 40 − 10 = 30 km/h

⇒ Time to cover 15 km upstream = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed

⇒ Time = 15 ÷ 30 = 1/2 hour

∴ The correct answer is 1/2 hour.

Additional Information

Speed in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: B = (D + U) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream

It is half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: S = (D − U) ÷ 2

Average Speed of Journey

If a boat goes a certain distance downstream and comes back upstream, the average speed is (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

questions.question: Which of the following is/are prime numbers? (i) 241 (ii) 337 (iii) 391 (iv) 571
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following is/are prime numbers?

(i) 241

(ii) 337

(iii) 391

(iv) 571
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To check if n is prime, test its divisibility by primes p ≤ √n.

(i) √241 ≈ 15.5: Not divisible by primes 7, 11, or 13 → Prime.

(ii) √337 ≈ 18.3: Not divisible by primes 7, 11, 13, or 17 → Prime.

(iii) 391 ÷ 17 = 23 → Composite; (iv) √571 ≈ 23.9: No prime factors ≤ 23 → Prime.

∴ The correct answer is (i), (ii) and (iv).

Alternate Method

Given numbers: (i) 241, (ii) 337, (iii) 391, (iv) 571.

Method: A number is prime if it is not divisible by any prime number less than or equal to its square root.

⇒ For 241: √241 ≈ 15.5. Primes to check: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13. Divisibility check: 241 ÷ 7 = 34.4, 241 ÷ 11 = 21.9, 241 ÷ 13 = 18.5. No factors found, so 241 is Prime.

⇒ For 337: √337 ≈ 18.3. Primes: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17. Divisibility check: 337 ÷ 13 = 25.9, 337 ÷ 17 = 19.8. No factors found, so 337 is Prime.

⇒ For 391: √391 ≈ 19.7. Primes up to 19: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. Checking divisibility: 391 ÷ 17 = 23. Since 17 is a factor, 391 is Composite.

⇒ For 571: √571 ≈ 23.9. Primes up to 23: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23. Divisibility check: 571 ÷ 19 = 30.05, 571 ÷ 23 = 24.8. No factors found, so 571 is Prime.

⇒ The prime numbers in the list are 241, 337, and 571.

∴ The correct answer is (i), (ii) and (iv).

Additional Information

Prime and Composite Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. A composite number has more than two factors. 1 is neither prime nor composite.

Even Prime Number

2 is the smallest prime number and the only even prime number in the entire number system.

Square Root Rule for Primality

To check if a number N is prime, we only need to test its divisibility by prime numbers up to √N. If no prime factor is found in this range, the number is prime.
